title: Domain-Specific Data Synthesis for LLMs through Minimal Sufficient Representation Learning

problem.claim: High-quality data for target domains is difficult to acquire.

gap.claim: Existing deductive synthesis methods depend on explicit natural-language domain descriptions and careful prompt engineering, limiting use when domains are difficult to articulate.

contributions.claim: DOMINO learns a minimal sufficient domain representation from reference samples and uses it to guide generation of domain-aligned synthetic data.
DOMINO combines prompt tuning with contrastive disentanglement to separate domain-level patterns from sample-specific noise.
The authors prove that DOMINO expands the support of the synthetic data distribution.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DOMINO as a novel framework and characterize the work as establishing a new paradigm for domain-specific data synthesis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On challenging coding benchmarks with implicit domain definitions, fine-tuning on DOMINO-synthesized data improves Pass@1 accuracy by up to 4.63% over strong instruction-tuned backbones.
The authors report that DOMINO demonstrates effectiveness and robustness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fine-tuning on domain-specific data can improve LLM performance in specific domains.
High-quality target-domain data is difficult to obtain.
Deductive synthesis methods rely on explicit domain descriptions and prompt engineering, which are unsuitable for difficult-to-articulate domains.
DOMINO uses reference examples to learn a minimal sufficient domain representation and guide domain-aligned synthesis.
The authors report theoretical diversity guarantees and improved coding-benchmark Pass@1 accuracy.

source_observation.claim: Reference examples can define a target domain when natural-language descriptions are difficult to formulate.

interpretation.claim: Inductive domain representation learning may reduce dependence on manual domain specification.

application.claim: For implicit domains, use representative samples to condition data synthesis and downstream adaptation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach works beyond the reported challenging coding benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract omits the specific benchmark datasets, sample sizes, baseline configurations, and statistical details.
The abstract does not state the conditions or proof details for the support-expansion result.
The abstract does not provide implementation details needed to assess reproducibility.
